name: Jaipur
overview: Rajasthan's capital, a planned 18th-century city painted terracotta-pink, famous for Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal and Jantar Mantar.

name: Udaipur
overview: A romantic lake city set around Lake Pichola, ringed by the Aravalli hills and the sprawling City Palace of Mewar.

name: Jaisalmer
overview: A living fort city of golden sandstone rising from the Thar Desert, gateway to camel safaris and desert music.

name: Amritsar
overview: Spiritual capital of Sikhism, home to the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) and the world's largest langar.

name: Chandigarh
overview: A modernist planned city designed by Le Corbusier, known for the Rock Garden and Sukhna Lake.

name: Patiala
overview: A former princely state famous for the Patiala peg, the Patiala salwar, and Qila Mubarak.

name: Agra
overview: Former Mughal capital on the Yamuna, home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and nearby Fatehpur Sikri.

name: Varanasi
overview: One of the world's oldest living cities, where the ghats of the Ganga host cremations, aarti and centuries of pilgrimage.

name: Lucknow
overview: Capital of Awadhi refinement — chikankari embroidery, kebabs, and the grand Bara Imambara.

name: Bodh Gaya
overview: The site where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree; a UNESCO World Heritage pilgrimage centre.

name: Patna
overview: Bihar's capital on the Ganga, once the seat of the Mauryan empire, now home to Sikh and Mauryan heritage.

name: Nalanda
overview: Ruins of the great 5th-century Mahavihara university, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that once taught 10,000 students.

name: New Delhi
overview: The seat of India's government, with Lutyens' boulevards, India Gate, Humayun's Tomb and the Lotus Temple.

name: Old Delhi
overview: The walled Mughal city of Shah Jahan — the Red Fort, Jama Masjid, and the food-and-spice labyrinth of Chandni Chowk.
